title: Nimzo-Indian Defense: Sämisch Variation
line: White takes the two bishops at the cost of doubled pawns, and Black attacks the front one.

steps.text: The Nimzo-Indian, and White pushes the pawn on a2 at once, to ask the bishop what it will do.
Take the knight with check. White gets the two bishops, but its pawns end up two on one file.
Push the pawn on c7 two squares. Now the pawn on c4 cannot move on, and Black can attack it.
Bring the other knight out. It attacks White's pawn on d4.
Castle, to get your king to safety.
Move the pawn on b7 one square. Your bishop can then come out against the pawn on c4.
White's pawn on e4 can push on and hit your knight. Step it back first. It also frees the pawn on f7.
Bring the bishop out against the pawn on c4.
Push the pawn on f7 two squares. It stops White's pawns from rolling on toward your king.

summary: White gets two bishops and doubled pawns. Black fixes the pawns, attacks the front one and blocks the king's side.
